Why McAllen businesses miss calls

McAllen is a shopping and health care center for the Rio Grande Valley and draws customers from northern Mexico. Education and health care employ more than a quarter of workers, and retail over 13%. Seasonal visitors known as Winter Texans add another wave of calls each year. A business here can get English, Spanish and mixed-language callers in the same hour, including people calling from across the border.

Which McAllen businesses benefit most?

  • Medical offices: Handle patient calls from across the Valley in English or Spanish.
  • Dental offices: Many patients travel in, so clear booking details help.
  • Restaurants: Answer questions and book tables during weekend shopping rushes.

What a call could sound like in McAllen

Here is an example of how a call might go. Your script, rules and wording would be set up with you.

Caller: Vengo de Reynosa el sábado. ¿Tienen citas disponibles?

AI receptionist: Replies in Spanish, books Saturday and shares your address and hours.

Does your McAllen AI receptionist need Spanish?

About 71.2% of McAllen residents age 5 and older speak Spanish at home. With about seven in ten residents speaking Spanish at home, Spanish should be standard for any McAllen business that takes calls. Can you keep your McAllen phone number?

Yes. McAllen callers will usually see the 956 area code, and you can keep the number customers already know. Forward it to the AI for all calls, only after hours, or only when your team does not pick up. We can also set up a new local number. Everything is set up remotely, so you do not need new equipment or a visit to an office.

What to check before you go live

  1. Test real calls: ask awkward questions, not only easy ones, and listen to how it handles them.
  2. Set the rules: decide which calls transfer to a person and which become messages.
  3. Plan your minutes: estimate your busiest month, not an average one.
  4. Tell callers what you need to: Texas is generally treated as a one-party consent state for recording calls, but rules differ for callers in other states, so check with your advisor if you record calls.
